actions.label: Investigate: Separate registration failure from first-menu activation

reproduce.title: PowerRename and File Locksmith context menu entries missing in v0.94.0 and later
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare reported 0.93 and 0.94+ behavior with the current supported build
prerequisites: A Windows 10 environment matching the original report; a separate ARM64 environment for the later symptom.
Use supported installation packages, not replacement binaries or registry scripts.
reproduce.expected_result: Both extensions remain available on supported installations; a first-show failure is distinguished from absent registration.
steps: Inspect normal package registration and open a file context menu after a fresh Explorer start on the Windows 10 setup.
Record PowerRename and File Locksmith independently before and after a supported reinstall.
On ARM64, open the first menu and then a second menu without restarting Explorer; record PowerRename and File Locksmith separately.

known_information: The original reporter supplies a diagnostic archive and says both PowerRename and File Locksmith entries disappeared from 0.94 onward.
Blocked-extension registry entries were already checked.
An ARM64 commenter describes intermittent PowerRename absence on the first menu even on 0.93 while File Locksmith works.
The newest commenter reports success after a registry/binary workaround and reinstall; that does not establish a general fix.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and public discussion, current ownership, labels and linked-work history.
Read all supplied version, architecture and workaround follow-ups, including the already answered registry check.
Checked current assignees and linked-work history rather than inferring ownership from a blank name.
Absence of one expected log message is not sufficient proof that shell registration failed.
inferences: Registration or Explorer package activation may explain the original both-entry failure, but the ARM64 first-show case may have a different mechanism.
issue_context.summary: The original Windows 10 shell-entry report and a later ARM64 first-menu intermittent report must remain distinct.
issue_context.analysis: Withdraw the old empty-assignee ownership claim and duplicate ZIP request. The useful next step is a maintainer comparison of registration and Explorer activation on the two reported configurations, not endorsing a binary/registry replacement.

fix_assessment.rationale: This is a scoped, confidence-qualified investigation/fix proposal, not an approved or independently converged implementation design.

judgment.rationale: Withdraw the old empty-assignee ownership claim and duplicate ZIP request. The useful next step is a maintainer comparison of registration and Explorer activation on the two reported configurations, not endorsing a binary/registry replacement.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the original Windows 10 both-entry failure separately from the ARM64 first-show symptom before choosing a registration or menu-activation fix.

title: PowerRename and File Locksmith context menu entries missing in v0.94.0 and later

confidence.rationale: The reports establish symptoms and useful distinctions but do not identify one shared failing registration path.

plan: Compare installed shell-package registration and Explorer activation for the original affected Windows 10 installation and a working baseline.
Run the ARM64 first-menu/reopen sequence independently and identify whether registration exists while activation is delayed.
Fix only the proven registration/activation boundary; preserve both shell extensions and avoid copying binaries or blindly rewriting registry keys.
proposed_fixes.title: Separate registration failure from first-menu activation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A per-user shell registration/Explorer activation mismatch is plausible for the original report, but cannot yet explain the distinct ARM64 first-show behavior.
verification: Both entries appear after a normal supported install and Explorer restart on the original supported configuration.
On ARM64, verify first and subsequent menus separately across repeated Explorer sessions.
